explanation: In German business culture, punctuality is a core sign of respect and professionalism; arriving late to a meeting without warning is seen as discourteous and suggests poor planning or disregard for others' time. Arriving a few minutes early is well regarded, and meetings tend to start and end on schedule.
local_tip: Aim to arrive 5-10 minutes early, and if you expect any delay, call or message ahead with an apology and your updated arrival time.

also_check.note: Arriving 15-30 minutes late to a business meeting is often tolerated and sometimes expected, as relationship-building is valued alongside punctuality.
Punctuality is taken extremely seriously; arriving late is a serious breach that can damage trust and business relationships.
Meetings may start later than scheduled due to hospitality norms and prayer times, but foreign visitors arriving on time is still seen as respectful.

sources.title: German business culture and etiquette - WeAreDevelopers
